label: workflow-verify.md:86 carries a wrong validate.sh contract and contradicts the document that owns it: the shared file says warnings 'only become a failing validation outcome under --strict, which exits 2 unless the folder is grandfathered', while validation-rules.md:44 says 'a warning stays advice in both modes and never changes the exit code. A rule that should block reports an error itself', and :159 says only SPECKIT_COMPLETION_FRESHNESS_ENFORCE escalates a stale-freshness warn to an error that makes --strict exit 2. The authority states it owns this meaning and that copies elsewhere go stale first (validation-rules.md:835). Reproducing case: the two rg commands print claims that cannot both be true. NEW P1.

The shared workflow trio and the repo rules carry the same floors twice with no pointer either way: reproduce/trace/one-cause in workflow-debug.md:50-57 vs root-cause-and-debugging.md:52-61; baseline/current/delta in workflow-verify.md:101-112 vs evidence-and-proof.md section 5; the mutation-check/negative-control ritual in workflow-verify.md:125-127 vs evidence-and-proof.md section 4; the pre-write restraint paragraph in workflow-implement.md:66 vs prevent-overengineering.md and AGENTS.md section 3. Every pair agrees in substance today, but the tiers load under different triggers, so a future edit can diverge unseen exactly as f-iter003-001 already did. Proposed repair: repo rules own the floors, shared files keep only the sk-code mechanism plus a one-line pointer. NEW P2.

The shared doctrine files carry surface-conditioned subsections while the hub's purity rule says shared material must never gain them: workflow-implement.md:78-84 and workflow-verify.md:76-99 embed 'OpenCode Surface Only' contracts (generate-context.js single-writer rule, sk-git boundary, validate.sh/tsc/rebuild-native chain) inside files symlinked into all three surfaces, while SKILL.md:163 says shared backend material 'must never gain per-mode workflow contracts' and sk-code-opencode already owns a shared tier (references/shared/alignment-verification-automation.md) where they can live. Reproducing case: rg -n 'OpenCode Surface Only' on the shared references prints four hits. NEW P2.

Verified as already consistent: the seven-rung ladder summary in workflow-implement.md:66 matches code-quality-standards.md:46-52 rung for rung including the reuse rung and the never-cut tail, and every repo-rule pair in f-iter003-002 agrees in substance today (reproduce, trace, one cause, whole-gate re-run, baseline, negative control). ALREADY-ADOPTED, no action beyond the pointer proposal.
